scope: Initial correctness and standalone full-content digests on three actual cached Harness blobs. No real restore or full-build performance claim.

controls.scope: Default-off output-only full-content hashing experiment: mode 0 original streaming, mode 1 bounded owned snapshot with serial hashing, mode 2 same snapshot with at most three additional hashing threads. 32–256 MiB inclusive; other outputs retain streaming. No input-digest, key, schema or materialization changes.
controls.run_gate: Complete the matched warm diagnostic first and confirm a warm output-validation wait of at least 25 ms. Correctness and standalone digest timing are insufficient for production adoption.

verification.limits: Initial implementation and standalone digests only; no real cache-hit request or full-project speed comparison yet. Initial sharded-file discovery failure retained.

recovery: Initial file discovery only searched top-level entries, but CAS blobs are sharded in 256 directories. Earlier build/unit/integration/15 canonical size checks passed. Their evidence and failed attempt are retained unchanged. Timing discovery now recurses through the dedicated blob directory.

host_activity.limits: Snapshots cover only the monitor interval. Known build-tool names and ancestry are heuristic; zero observations do not prove an idle machine. ps CPU values are platform-specific snapshots, not integrated CPU time. No command arguments, environments, executable paths or unrelated process IDs are retained. No samples are removed and no process is stopped.

decision: Keep default-off. Next compare actual large-output cache restores using the same binary at modes 0 and 2, with fresh references, preserved-mtime edits/corruption, stream and output byte/mode checks. Then repeat whole Harness against baseline and kache before adoption.
